title: Nephrolithiasis and nephrocalcinosis

steps.tx: **Calcium** stones account for approximately 75% to 80% of all nephrolithiasis cases, most commonly composed of calcium oxalate (monohydrate whewellite or dihydrate weddellite) and calcium phosphate (apatite or brushite). The image is calcium oxalate and uric acid crystals and stone morphology.

steps.tx: **Idiopathic hypercalciuria** (24-hour urine calcium > 250 mg in women, > 300 mg in men, or > 4 mg/kg/day) is the most prevalent metabolic risk factor for calcium nephrolithiasis, managed with dietary sodium restriction (< 2 g/day) and thiazide diuretics.

steps.tx: **Dietary calcium** restriction paradoxically increases calcium oxalate stone formation by enhancing uncomplexed free oxalate absorption in the gut; patients are advised to maintain normal dietary calcium intake (1000 to 1200 mg/day) taken with meals. The first step is Thiazide inhibits NCC in distal convoluted tubule.

steps.tx: **Uric acid stones** form exclusively in persistently acidic urine (urine pH < 5.5) where insoluble un-ionized uric acid predominates, appearing radiolucent on conventional plain radiography but readily detectable on non-contrast CT (200 to 400 Hounsfield units). One side is Acidic Urine (pH < 5.5), and the other side is Alkaline Urine (pH 6.5 to 7.0).
steps.say: Uric acid stones form exclusively in persistently acidic urine (urine pH less than 5 point 5) where insoluble un-ionized uric acid predominates, appearing radiolucent on conventional plain radiography but readily detectable on non-contrast CT (200 to 400 Hounsfield units). One side is Acidic Urine (pH less than 5 point 5), and the other side is Alkaline Urine (pH 6 point 5 to 7 point 0).

steps.tx: Therapeutic urinary alkalinization with **potassium citrate** (targeting a urine pH of 6.5 to 7.0) is the cornerstone of uric acid stone chemolysis and prevention, while allopurinol or febuxostat is added if hyperuricosuria or hyperuricemia persists. The image is staghorn calculus in renal pelvis and percutaneous nephrolithotomy techniques.

steps.tx: **Struvite stones** (infection stones, magnesium ammonium phosphate and carbonate apatite) form in alkaline urine (pH > 7.2) infected by urease-producing organisms (Proteus mirabilis, Klebsiella, Pseudomonas), producing branched staghorn calculi. One side is Pathophysiology, and the other side is Diagnostic Findings.

steps.tx: **Cystinuria** is an autosomal recessive defect in the dibasic amino acid transporter SLC3A1 (rBAT) or SLC7A9, presenting in young patients with pathognomonic flat hexagonal crystals in acidic urine, positive sodium cyanide-nitroprusside test, and radiopaque ground-glass stones. The first step is Cystine excretion exceeds solubility threshold.

steps.tx: **Medullary sponge kidney** is a congenital non-inherited malformation characterized by cystic dilatation of the collecting ducts in one or more renal pyramids, strongly predisposing to recurrent nephrolithiasis, distal RTA, and medullary nephrocalcinosis. The paired value for Medullary nephrocalcinosis is > 95% of cases.
